Fastmail is fantastic, I've been a very happy customer for at least a couple years now. Masked emails have been so nice for throwaway/sketchy sites. It's done everything I could ask.

Fastmail is the service I've paid for longer than any other, without any pauses, and with the most satisfaction of any subscription... it works perfectly for me and offers excellent value for what I pay. It's so gratifyingly functional and boring.
Been about 10 years now and it is the definition of 'It just works'. I like that they are up front with how the data is handled and what that can mean for privacy.
As an alternative to forwarding, you can configure Fastmail to fetch mail from (and send via) Gmail like a mail client.

Uses a Google Workspace account for their custom domain while email for that domain stays at Fastmail, and it works fine. The only hassle is the calendar: you can add your Fastmail calendar to Google Calendar, but Google is slow to sync.
Migration workflow: set up a filter on Fastmail showing all mail delivered to the old @gmail.com address in the last two weeks, then periodically went through it to unsubscribe or change addresses.

Switching is an easy process these days, just insanely time consuming. Fastmail has an easy migration tool if you don't want to go the IMAP route. Migrating filters and rules over, on the other hand...

Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP. Fastmail isn't really intended for this since the limits don't scale to large services, but it works well enough.
Switched from ProtonMail to Fastmail recently. Fastmail was a ton faster and didn't randomly forget my sessions. Night and day to use. It also let me use two custom domains without paying twice.

Switched primary email to Fastmail a few months ago. Wanted something that works well, is paid with proper support, allows custom domains, and is cheapest. Fastmail fit the bill and is working as expected.

Used Fastmail as part of a DeGoogle effort and is very happy with it; mail gets delivered to recipients' inboxes. However, as an Australian service it raises privacy/five-eyes concerns, a price they accepted because business mail must arrive.
Loved the product and the company but left because they couldn't accept data being under both Australian and American jurisdictions; says privacy claims are aspirational given hosting locations.
Was very pleasantly surprised how easy the move from Google services to Fastmail was (with domain managed by Cloudflare).
On spam filtering: 'Actually really good. I've just checked my spam folder and it's full - nothing has made it through.' Another user: 'I pretty much never see spam.'

Criticism of Fastmail's new EU (Amsterdam) region: they state they can't guarantee data remains only in the EU, so commenters say businesses with strict data-residency requirements won't touch it and it misses why people want EU hosting.
Recently moved email to FastMail and really likes it, even preferring its web interface over Gmail's.
FastMail is an upgrade from Gmail. Good enough that after swearing never to pay for webmail, I remain a paying customer after 10+ years.

Complaint: text smileys like ':)' get replaced by yellow emoji icons (in plain-text view); support seemed uninterested in adding an option to disable it. Another user made a Stylish userstyle to hide them. Otherwise 'an excellent, excellent service.'
Critic notes that FastMail's Android app relies on Google Cloud Messaging for push, so users leaving Gmail for privacy still depend on Google for functionality.
